items.summary:
Accelerated journey of AI-native startups

Vietnam’s AI-native startups are outpacing their peers. Free from legacy IT, they are shipping AI-powered products that scale faster and reach further. As a result, these cloud-first startups have reported 147 per cent average annual revenue growth in the past year. [...] According to AWS, Vietnam’s businesses have ambitions to transform with AI, with 69 per cent of businesses saying AI adoption is a top or high priority, and 84 per cent expect their use of AI to increase over the next year. This adoption spans large enterprises, small and medium-size enterprises, and AI-native startups, with each of them having their own priorities and needs. Even though 61 per cent of AI adopters say they're still experimenting, the early returns are promising with 71 per cent [...] NoteX is an AI-powered voice intelligence and speech platform built in Vietnam and scaling globally. Running on AWS, it has reduced its AI processing costs and latency by 30 per cent and scaled to over one million users across Vietnam and over 20 countries in its first year.

Drylab AI, a startup founded by three Vietnamese entrepreneurs, has raised $3 million to develop AI agents that help laboratories and pharmaceutical companies retain scientific knowledge and learn from past experiments.

Founded in 2025 by John Phan, Henry Phan and Nhi Nguyen, Drylab AI operates in Singapore and San Francisco, the United States. [...] Drylab's ambition goes beyond helping scientists learn how to use AI.

It aims to enable research organizations to build intelligence systems that progressively develop a deeper understanding of their scientific work.

The startup also illustrates how Vietnamese technology entrepreneurs are moving into highly specialized areas of the global research and development market, tackling complex challenges at the intersection of artificial intelligence, biotechnology and pharmaceutical research. [...] From left: Benedict Tan of Vertex Ventures, Drylab Chief Science Officer Nhi Nguyen, Chief Technology Officer Huy Phan, CEO John Phan and Genping Liu of Vertex Ventures. Photo: Drylab.

 

A study published in "Nature" in early 2026, analyzing 41.3 million scientific papers, found that researchers using AI published 3.02 times as many papers as those who did not. However, the research also revealed a paradox: the overall range of scientific topics being explored was narrowing.

items.summary:
A new way to measure how AI agents handle the routine analyses of wet-lab science—BioBasicsBench.

Developed with Ligo, a biotech company focused on enzyme design, the benchmark draws on 100 tasks from real experiments to test whether agents can interpret raw lab data, identify errors, and recognize when the evidence doesn’t support a conclusion.

Accelerating biological research starts with getting the everyday work right. BioBasicsBench shows where models need to improve, and helps us track what those gains mean for scientific progress, biosafety, and biosecurity.

items.title: (Allegedly)
items.summary:
(Allegedly) 
NVIDIA has been secretly running your GPU at 50% speed for AI.

A developer on GitHub just unlocked the other 50% for free.

No BIOS flash. No custom drivers. No hardware mods.

Here is the crazy truth:
Consumer GeForce RTX cards (20, 30, and 40 series) use the exact same silicon as NVIDIA's $5,000+ enterprise cards. 

To protect their datacenter margins, NVIDIA artificially capped consumer Tensor Cores to HALF speed on FP16, BF16, and TF32 math.

A new open-source project called "gpu-unlock" removes that artificial cap at boot before the NVIDIA driver even loads.

Look at the BF16 compute jump on stock power limits:
• RTX 3060 12GB: 27 -> 51 TFLOPS (+87%)
• RTX 3070: 40 -> 72 TFLOPS (+81%)
• RTX 3080: 65 -> 113 TFLOPS (+73%)
• RTX 3090: 75 -> 125 TFLOPS (+65%)
• RTX 4080: 104 -> 193 TFLOPS (+87%)
• RTX 4090: 165 -> 329 TFLOPS (+100% peak rate)

Real-world AI speedups (with bit-identical outputs):
• +25–55% faster LLM prompt processing / prefill (vLLM, PyTorch)
• +30–55% faster image generation (ComfyUI, SDXL, DiT)
• +25–50% faster LoRA & BF16 fine-tuning
• +50–60% faster FlashAttention kernels

---
Quick pause—If you want more high-leverage drops like this:
• Follow @autoaiadvantage > https://t.co/Bp89dBjzms if you're interested in AI agents, local LLMs, tech, robotics & automation.
• Follow @emanuelebashuri > https://t.co/HBFWqQ2Cn8 if you're interested in holistic health, wealth building, family values & GG33 numerology.
---

How it works:
It loads a tiny Linux kernel module in initramfs that flips the hardware speed selectors (SS0 0x88888888) back to full rate, resets the card in ~1 second, and lets the untouched stock NVIDIA driver take over. (There's also a community Windows port in the FAQ).

3 lines to install on Linux:
git clone https://t.co/jXDGFL4t8t
cd gpu-unlock
make install

Then add gpu_unlock.targets=all to your kernel cmdline and reboot.

results.facts: - Lab transcripts can be submitted only if they do not contain secrets or personal data. - Tool results should be summarized with source links, not copied wholesale when sensitive content is present.

results.title: Data Privacy Policy For AI Tools
results.facts: - Do not paste confidential customer data, access tokens, unreleased financials, or private employee information into external AI tools. - Redact personally identifiable information before using live web, model, or scraping tools. - If the user asks to process confidential data, ask for a redacted version or use an approved internal workflow.

results.title: Data Privacy Policy For AI Tools
results.facts: - API keys must stay in `.env` or a secret manager. - Never include API keys in prompts, transcripts, reports, screenshots, or git commits. - If a key is exposed, rotate it before continuing the lab.
